significance: A Divya Desam that stands inside the precinct of the Ekambareswarar Shiva temple, one of the very few Vishnu shrines of the 108 housed within a Shaiva complex. First raised under the Pallavas, it was rebuilt by the Cholas with later Vijayanagara-era additions.
story: Vishnu is said to have cooled Parvati's fiery penance here with rays reflected from the crescent moon on Shiva's head, earning the name Nilathingal Thundam.
